newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS - Austria's AMS reports poor earnings.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Austria's AMS reports poor earnings.

text.p: A miserable batch of nine-month earnings from microchip-maker Austria Mikro Systeme on Thursday prompted a rush of selling in Vienna as investors took fright at the spectre that worse was still to come.
"1996 will certainly not be the year for AMS," finance director Johann Stritzelberger told Reuters.
AMS stock fell five percent on the earnings figures in an buoyant overall market, making it by far Vienna's worst performer this morning.

The AMS group turned in a pre-tax profit of just 58 million schillings ($5.5 million) as losses at its two majority-owned acquisitions amid a floundering global semiconductor market continued to take their toll.
Comparative group figures were not made available by the company because of the consolidation of its two subsidiaries SAMES and Thesys, acquired in late 1995.

In the parent company, pre-tax profit slumped 32.7 percent to 148 million schillings -- just 20 million above that posted in the first six months of this year -- while sales fell 26.6 percent to 989.6 million schillings.

"These are pretty disappointing figures as they show a continuation of the negative trend," said Gerhard Auer, analyst at London-based ICE Securities, adding he holds out scant hope of an improvement in the fourth quarter.
This view was reflected on the market, where AMS stock was the most actively traded, standing 31.9 schillings lower at 689.0 in midday trade.
"The old low of 650 schillings is once again within reach," said one trader.
Pundits voiced concern above all at the continuing downturn in the company's order over the last three quarters.
In the parent, incoming orders fell 40.5 percent to 789 million schillings while the order backlog stood 52.1 percent lower at 346.7 million schillings on September 30.
Group incoming orders for the first nine months reached 996.1 million schillings while the order backlog stood at 583.7 million schillings.

Investors' hopes of evidence that AMS was coming to grips with turning around its two subsidiaries were dashed as its 51.25 percent-owned Thesys Gesellschaft fuer Mikroelektronik GmbH in Germany turned in a loss of 155.4 million compared to a loss of 83.9 million posted in the the first half of 1996.
AMS' 51-percent owned South African Micro-Electronic Systems Ltd (SAMES) suffered a loss of 77.6 million schillings compared with a loss of 64.9 million in the first six months.

But finance director Stritzelberger stressed the company's streamlining measures and its restructuring of the two silicon foundries into ASIC (application specific integrated circuits) producers were running to schedule. ($1=10.61 Schilling)
